description: Django 4.2 removes support for using RawSQL() aggregations on MySQL 8+ because MySQL 8+ supports functional dependencies in GROUP BY clauses, eliminating the need for the workaround. Applications using RawSQL() in aggregations will fail. Standard aggregation functions must be used instead.

conditions.statement: Target Django version is 4.2 or higher

evidence.quote_or_summary: MySQL 8+ allows functional dependencies on GROUP BY columns, so the pre-Django 4.2 workaround of grouping by primary keys of the main table is removed. As a consequence, using RawSQL() aggregations is no longer supported on MySQL
evidence.relevance: States RawSQL() aggregations removed in Django 4.2

conditions.statement: Application uses RawSQL() in aggregation queries on MySQL

evidence.quote_or_summary: using RawSQL() aggregations is no longer supported on MySQL as there is no way to determine if such aggregations are needed or valid in the GROUP BY clause. Use aggregation-functions instead.
evidence.relevance: Explains the removal and directs to use standard aggregation functions

conditions.statement: Application is running on MySQL 8 or higher

evidence.quote_or_summary: MySQL 8+ allows functional dependencies on GROUP BY columns
evidence.relevance: Indicates this issue applies to MySQL 8+

suggested_actions: Search codebase for RawSQL() usage: grep -r 'RawSQL' --include='*.py'
Identify RawSQL() usage in aggregation contexts (e.g., .annotate(), .aggregate())
Replace RawSQL() aggregations with standard Django aggregation functions
Test queries on MySQL 8+ to verify correct GROUP BY behavior

path_name: JSONField with encoded JSON strings triggers deprecation warnings
description: Passing JSON-encoded string literals to JSONField and associated lookups/aggregates is deprecated in Django 4.2. In 4.2, encoded strings will be decoded with a warning. In Django 5.1+, string literals will be interpreted as JSON string literals. Code must be updated to pass non-encoded values.

conditions.statement: Target Django version is 4.2 or higher

evidence.quote_or_summary: JSONField and its associated lookups and aggregates used to allow passing JSON encoded string literals which caused ambiguity on whether string literals were already encoded from database backend's perspective. During the deprecation period string literals will be attempted to be JSON decoded and a warning will be emitted on success
evidence.relevance: States the deprecation of encoded JSON strings

conditions.statement: Application passes JSON-encoded strings to JSONField or related operations

evidence.quote_or_summary: Code that used to pass JSON encoded string literals: Document(data=Value('"null"')), Document(data=Value('"[]"')), Document(data=Value('"\"foo-bar\""'))

suggested_actions: Search for JSONField usage with Value(): grep -r 'JSONField.*Value\|Value.*JSONField' --include='*.py'
Look for encoded JSON strings like Value('"null"'), Value('[]'), etc.
Replace encoded strings with native Python values: None, [], 'foo-bar', etc.
For Value() with JSON, use Value(None, JSONField()) instead of Value('"null"')
Test JSONField queries and aggregations after changes
